title: Port scanning with nmap
summary: Discover hosts on a network you are allowed to test, find their open ports, and identify what is running.

nodes.target: a server somewhere in 10.15.1.0/24 (you have to find it)

tasks.title: Who is out there?
tasks.text: From **scanner**, find the live hosts on `10.15.1.0/24`. One of them runs a **web server on port 80**. What is its IP address?
hints: `nmap -sn 10.15.1.0/24` finds live hosts without scanning ports.
Then check port 80 across the whole range: `nmap -p 80 --open 10.15.1.0/24`.

tasks.title: All the doors
tasks.text: By default nmap only checks the 1,000 most common ports. Scan **every** TCP port on the web server. How many are open?

tasks.title: The odd one out
tasks.text: Three of the open ports are well known. One is a high, non-standard port that a default scan would have missed. Which port number is it?
hints: Look at your full scan from t2. Well-known ports are below 1024; 3306 is MySQL.

tasks.title: What version?
tasks.text: Services often announce themselves in a **banner** when you connect. Which version number does the FTP server on port 21 advertise?
hints: Or read the banner yourself: `nc <ip> 21` (Ctrl+C to quit).

tasks.title: Talk to the unknown service
tasks.text: Connect to the non-standard port with `nc` and see what it does. Get the flag out of it.
hints: `nc <ip> <port>` opens a raw connection. Type into it and press Enter.
The service tells you to send `HELP`.
